title: The attack surface of an LLM application

videos.script: An application built on a model is more than the model. There is the chat box, the documents it reads, the tools it can call, the logs it writes and the company that runs the model. {{title}} Every one of those is a place where text comes in or goes out. Together they are the attack surface, and this lesson is about drawing it before anybody else does. {{surface}} The difficulty is particular to models. A model reads its instructions and the text it is given as one stream, and it cannot reliably tell them apart. {{stream}} So the question for every entry point is the same. Who wrote this text, and what can it reach? {{question}} In the lab, Tarefa's assistant has ten entry points, written down in one file. Each says whether it is trusted, and which control covers it. {{inventory}} One has no control at all. The map's first job is to show that, so that it gets fixed rather than found. {{gap}}
